purpose: V6 blind text scenarios; provide only user_request and raw_inputs to executors. Actual local production/continuity tests are recorded separately outside reusable fixtures.

cases.user_request: Develop a four-scene outline from these materials and update our compact adaptation/source decision record. Choose the relevant workflow profile and explain which checks matter now. Preserve my preference for a voluntary choice and a companion with agency. Include a short proposed afterword note distinguishing our adaptation from the supplied versions. Outline-stage text only, under 650 words. No research, illustration or production work.

raw_inputs.brief-F2.txt: Original-world retelling for a standalone teen novella. Rian and companion Osa need to cross the fictional Glass Lake before the town's lamps go out. Dry warmth, no prescribed chapter count. The traveler must make a voluntary consequential choice; Osa must have her own aim and meaningful action. Working preference: the route around the lake interests me more than purchasing passage. No selected source version or outline yet. Today only four scenes and an adaptation record; final prose/art/formats are undecided.
raw_inputs.source-A-excerpt.txt: Supplied excerpt labeled The Glass Lake, edition A, anonymous fictional tale, translation/edition date not supplied: The ferryman asked the traveler for their name as payment. The traveler refused and walked around the lake, arriving after the lamps went dark. Only this excerpt is available; no full text or evidence of historical precedence is supplied.
raw_inputs.source-B-note.txt: Supplied teacher's note describing edition B of the same fictional tale: The traveler paid a glass coin for passage and forgot the road home. The note does not quote B's actual wording. Its original edition and translator are unavailable. This is a secondary account; no independent verification has occurred.
raw_inputs.existing-source-record.txt: SRC-A: supplied excerpt, read status not yet recorded. SRC-B: teacher note, read status not yet recorded. Old planning line says: 'The traditional version requires a coin and a name, then the traveler loses the road home.' This line was an unsourced combination of the two accounts. No claim about an actual culture or historical tradition is intended. Keep SRC-A/SRC-B IDs and the accepted brief preferences.

observable_behaviors: Produces four usable causal scenes with voluntary consequence, meaningful independent companion agency and an ending response to the lost light; new story details are labeled creative adaptation rather than sourced facts.
Selects a composable standalone/retelling/outline profile and limits records/checks to present needs; no fabricated print facts or mandatory art/production tasks.
Retains SRC-A/SRC-B and distinguishes actual excerpt reading from secondary-note reading and inaccessible original B; no fresh full-source read or cultural authority claim.
Corrects the combined traditional claim, preserves both variants separately, explains the bounded working adaptation choice against the brief, and keeps provenance/edition uncertainties visible.

Provides an actual short afterword proposal with accurate limited attribution and a source-to-decision-to-outline destination trail; does not imply the note is a verified quotation or choose authenticity by unsupported age/authority.
Reports actual outline/source comparison coverage and relevant completion checks, with unresolved later prose/reader/production validation left pending.
evaluator_only.evidence_scope: New outline and source/adaptation record from supplied invented texts; no original books, vault, external research, culture consultation, art or production output.

cases.user_request: Fix the flashback passage and reconcile the conflicting scene/state notes. Preserve the accepted present-day material and the reveal in reading position 5. Give me the revised flashback, corrected compact continuity/knowledge entries, affected checks and source-use disclosure. Text only, under 650 words. Do not rewrite other scenes or pretend a whole manuscript or checker run occurred.

raw_inputs.foundation-F7.txt: Close third through Mara. Entity M. Topic KEY-HOLDER: her brother held the brass key; the reader first learns this in reading position 5. A character can know before the narration discloses it, but narration must preserve the stated reader boundary. Story-time values are ordinal chronology, not page numbers. Scope is this novella only.
raw_inputs.accepted-canon.txt: D-CLOAK: M wears amber from story_time 0 inclusive until 20 exclusive; slate blue from 20 onward. D-KNOW: M learns KEY-HOLDER at story_time 25; she does not know it earlier. The holder fact itself concerns an earlier event and does not establish when M knows it. All values are supplied fictional canon. Osa's clothing is not described and stays unknown.
raw_inputs.scene-map.txt: S1: story_time 30, read_order 1, present day, M's slate-blue cloak; she privately knows KEY-HOLDER, but this scene does not reveal it to the reader. S2: story_time 10, read_order 3, flashback, draft below. S5: story_time 26, read_order 5, established first reader disclosure of KEY-HOLDER. S1/S5 are accepted and not supplied as full text. Old flat sheet: 'M always wears blue; everyone knows her brother took the key.' This sheet conflicts with the dated canon and overstates others' knowledge.
raw_inputs.S2-draft.txt: Mara drew her slate-blue cloak around her and waited beside the empty hook. Her brother had the brass key; she had known it for years. She turned the ledger so the rain would miss its pages, then carried it to Osa at the gate.
raw_inputs.check-history.txt: R-S1: supplied record says S1 checked for concealment/appearance under F7, passed. R-S5: supplied record says the position-5 reveal checked, passed. There is no recorded S2 review, no full-text read and no structured JSON ledger/checker report. No image asset, recap or profile is provided.

observable_behaviors: Actually revises S2 to amber and removes premature knowledge/disclosure while preserving the hook, protection of ledger pages and delivery to Osa; adds no contradictory invented explanation.
Separates story chronology from reading order; S2 uses state at time 10 while audience disclosure is evaluated at reading position 3, with the first reveal remaining at 5.
Distinguishes event truth, Mara's acquisition of knowledge at 25 and reader knowledge; preserves S1's later-time blue cloak and private knowledge without forcing disclosure at reading position 1.
Replaces the universal flat-sheet claim with scoped intervals/entries and explicit unknowns for Osa/others; retains D-CLOAK/D-KNOW/M/KEY-HOLDER/S1/S2/S5 identities.

Attributes retained S1/S5 passes only to supplied prior records, scopes actual review to the excerpt and records, and leaves dependent asset/recap/profile checks pending if applicable rather than claiming they are unchanged or inspected.
Explains that structured continuity checks would evaluate explicit declarations only and does not claim a checker run, whole-book semantic verification or fresh vault consultation.
evaluator_only.evidence_scope: Actual local passage rewrite and manual temporal/knowledge reasoning over supplied records; no full manuscript, generated ledger validation, images or platform actions.
